rounds.text: Redington Ltd presents a compelling value opportunity, trading at a modest P/E of 17.4x while delivering exceptional operational efficiency, evidenced by an ROCE of 18.4% and ROE of 16.9% that comfortably outpace sector benchmarks [E1, E10, E12, E13]. The company is experiencing rapid fundamental acceleration, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 23% and an explosive 42% surge in compounded profit growth [E17, E21]. This robust expansion is further validated by a rules-based screen score of 92 out of 100, driven by extraordinary recent gains including a 35% year-on-year rise in sales and a 94% year-on-year jump in net profit [E60, E61, E63]. Market participants are severely mispricing the company's future potential, as a reverse DCF demonstrates that today's price implies a mere 8.8% earnings growth rate, which is heavily discounted compared to the 16.0% base case assumption and leaves a substantial margin of safety [E47]. Conceded: cash conversion sits at a low 0.18x with operating cash flow representing only 32% of operating profit [E34, E37].

The valuation and price momentum are stretched to an extreme, sitting right at 100% of the 52-week range and 0.0% away from the 52-week high with an extended momentum reading [E48, E49, E66]. The stock has outrun its own five-year fundamentals as share prices grew 23% against 16% profit growth, creating a clear price-led divergence [E56]. Underlying cash generation is severely disconnected from reported accounting profits, shown by an alarming cash conversion ratio of just 0.18x and operating cash flow representing a mere 32% of operating profit as of March 2026 [E34, E37]. This massive gap between earnings and actual cash points to troubling accruals and surging receivables that demand close scrutiny [E34]. Furthermore, institutional money flow registers as negative with domestic institutional holdings declining from 17.38% to 16.37% alongside a recorded institutional outflow signal [E43, E44, E65]. Compounded profit growth over three years has also slowed to a modest 5%, highlighting inconsistent underlying expansion relative to short-term spikes [E20]. Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 17.4x with a solid 1.50% dividend yield and boasts a healthy long-term return on equity [E1, E4, E26].

Conceded: the price sits 100% of the way up its 52-week range and 0.0% from its high [E48, E49], and share price growth has outpaced five-year profit growth [E56]. However, this momentum is thoroughly backed by exceptional fundamental acceleration, including a TTM sales growth surge of 23% and a staggering 42% TTM profit growth [E17, E21], backed by screen reasons highlighting recent YoY sales up 35% and net profit soaring 94% [E61, E63]. While the cash conversion ratio of 0.18x warrants observation [E34], it is paired with actual operating cash flow of Rs 231 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 125 Cr [E35, E36], alongside a conservatively financed balance sheet carrying a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28x [E38]. Conceded: domestic institutional holdings saw a slight dip [E43], but foreign institutions aggressively increased their stake to 61.96% [E42]. Finally, the three-year profit slowdown [E20] is completely eclipsed by top-tier capital efficiency metrics, boasting an 18.4% ROCE and a 16.9% ROE that vastly outperform sector benchmarks [E12, E13, E10, E9].

Conceded: foreign institutions aggressively increased their stake to 61.96% [E42]. However, the bull's reliance on TTM profit growth of 42% [E21] masks a severe qualitative breakdown: operating cash flow for March 2026 was a meager 32% of operating profit, yielding an alarming cash conversion ratio of 0.18x that explicitly flags receivables and accrual risks [E34, E37]. Conceded: ROCE stands at 18.4% and ROE at 16.9% [E12, E13]. Yet, the bull ignores that the stock is trading at a premium P/E of 20.16x and EV/EBITDA of 12.23x against sector benchmarks [E6, E11], while domestic institutional holdings have declined [E43] alongside negative institutional money flow [E44]. Conceded: the price sits 100% up its 52-week range [E48]. But this momentum is classified as price-led where 5-year price growth of 23% outpaced 5-year profit growth of 16% [E56], and the asset carries a historical peak-to-trough drawdown risk of -80.2% coupled with high annualised volatility of 42.7% [E53, E54]. Finally, borrowings have ticked upward to Rs 2,842 Cr [E40], and operating margins remain stagnant at an inconsistent 2% with zero expansion over trailing and quarterly periods [E30, E31, E32, E33].

Conceded: operating cash flow for March 2026 was 32% of operating profit, yielding a cash conversion ratio of 0.18x [E34, E37]. However, the bear's claim of a severe qualitative breakdown is offset by the trailing twelve month profit growth of 42% and strong recent sales growth of 35% YoY [E21, E61]. Conceded: the P/E of 20.16x and EV/EBITDA of 12.23x sit above sector benchmarks [E6, E11], and domestic institutional holdings declined [E43]. Yet, the core valuation model reveals an intrinsic value of Rs 678 per share, establishing a substantial 41.0% margin of safety against the current market price [E45, E46]. Furthermore, the company commands a superior ROE of 16.9% and an ROCE of 18.4% [E12, E13], completely outperforming the broader sector benchmarks of 4.86% and 6.54% respectively [E9, E10]. Conceded: historical volatility is 42.7% and the max drawdown reached -80.2% [E53, E54]. Despite this, foreign institutions have actively increased their stake to 61.96% [E42], and a rules-based screen scores the business at a high 92 out of 100 with a medium confidence buy rating [E60].

Conceded: foreign institutions increased their stake to 61.96% [E42]. However, the bull's reliance on high TTM profit growth of 42% and 35% YoY sales growth ignores that price has outpaced fundamentals with a price-led 5-year trend where price grew 23% versus profit at 16% [E21, E56, E61]. Conceded: intrinsic value of Rs 678 offers a margin of safety [E45, E46], but this projection clashes with the reality of negative institutional money flow and a domestic institutional holding drop to 16.37% [E43, E44]. Furthermore, the bull points to superior ROCE of 18.4% and ROE of 16.9% [E12, E13], yet downplays the alarming cash conversion ratio of 0.18x and operating cash flow at a mere 32% of operating profit in March 2026, signaling that reported profits are not translating into actual cash [E34, E37]. Conceded: a rules-based screen scores 92 out of 100 [E60], but the stock sits at 100% of its 52-week range and 0.0% away from its high while facing an inconsistent operating margin trend and a historical max drawdown of -80.2% [E32, E49, E53].
